Section 1: Business Model Transition Post-"Double Reduction" & Competitive Moat

Following the implementation of China's "Double Reduction" policy in July 2021—which banned profit-making curriculum tutoring for K-9 students—New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. (NYSE: EDU / 9901.HK) executed one of the most successful corporate turnarounds in global education history. Rather than liquidating its assets, management re-engineered the company's business model around non-academic enrichment, high school academic preparation, intelligent learning hardware, study-abroad consulting, and live-streaming e-commerce via East Buy (Dongfang Zhenxuan).

By FY2026 (fiscal year ended May 31, 2026), New Oriental completed its post-policy operational restructuring, achieving full-year revenues of $5,661.3 million (+15.5% YoY) and Q4 revenues of $1,529.5 million (+23.0% YoY). The firm's operational flywheel relies on four core economic moats that differentiate it from regional competitors:

  • 30-Year Brand Trust & Pricing Power: Built over three decades by founder Yu Minhong, the "New Oriental" brand retains premium mindshare among Chinese parents and adult learners. This goodwill enables EDU to command superior pricing power in non-academic tutoring (coding, arts, literacy, critical thinking) and high school test preparation without requiring high digital advertising spending.
  • Online-Merging-Offline (OMO) Infrastructure: EDU’s physical network of learning centers across approximately 60 Chinese cities serves as an asset-light distribution system. The OMO architecture digitizes course delivery, unifies student progress tracking, and allows hybrid offline-online cross-selling of learning tablets, study tours, and adult education offerings.
  • Proprietary Domain-Specific AI Ecosystem: Rather than relying on generic third-party large language models, EDU deployed a proprietary AI-powered personalized learning platform tailored strictly to its educational content assets. Deployed across learning devices and physical classrooms, this platform generated immediate monetization within 25 days of launch while delivering over $100 million in cost efficiencies across operating functions in FY2026.
  • Multi-Channel E-Commerce & Lifestyle Flywheel (East Buy): Operating 18 vertical live-streaming channels on Douyin and a standalone app, East Buy leverages knowledge-based live-streaming and high-quality private-label goods ("Three Highs": safety, quality, cost performance) to generate high-margin cash flows. The integration of physical "New Oriental Home" pilots within learning centers merges education services, direct-to-consumer goods, and cultural tourism into a single customer lifetime value (LTV) framework.

Section 3: Real Cash Flow & SBC Dilution Audit

A rigorous audit of New Oriental Education & Technology Group (NYSE: EDU) requires peeling back GAAP earnings to evaluate true cash generation, working capital mechanics, and stock-based compensation (SBC) dilution. Following Warren Buffett's intrinsic value principles, reported earnings often obscure economic reality when stock compensation is treated as a "non-cash charge" and negative working capital float is misunderstood. EDU presents an exceptional cash flow model powered by up-front customer collections and zero funded debt.

1. Deferred Tuition Float Dynamics & Working Capital Superiority

EDU operates a negative working capital economic engine similar to insurance float or subscription software. Tuition fees for K-12 non-academic tutoring, test preparation, and overseas consulting are collected upfront prior to service delivery. These funds are credited to Deferred Revenue on the balance sheet, which expanded by 14.8% YoY to reach $2.24 billion at the close of FY2026 (May 31, 2026).

The Berkshire Float Rule: Deferred tuition represents $2.24 billion of cost-free operational capital provided directly by parents and students. Because EDU collects cash months before recognizing revenue and paying teacher payroll, the company generates robust operating cash inflows ($518.7M in Q4 FY26 alone) that outstrip GAAP net income ($62.2M in Q4 FY26). This interest-free float effectively funds new learning center expansion and tech/AI infrastructure without requiring debt financing.

2. Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) & Owner Earnings Reconciliation

Management frequently highlights Non-GAAP Net Income ($571.1M in FY2026 vs. $475.2M GAAP) by adding back SBC and acquisition-related amortization. However, under fundamental principles, SBC is an authentic economic expense that dilutes existing equity holders. To establish true Warren Buffett Owner Earnings, SBC must be subtracted alongside Maintenance CapEx.

In Q4 FY2026, EDU generated $518.7 million in Net Cash Inflow from Operations against $99.0 million in Capital Expenditures (driven by opening 10–15% net new center capacity). Adjusting for estimated quarterly SBC yields true, normalized Owner Cash Generation:

Furthermore, management has transitioned into a highly shareholder-friendly capital return phase, blending cash dividends with stock repurchases.

As of May 31, 2026, EDU held $1.82 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $1.37 billion in short-term and non-current term deposits, and $2.37 billion in short-term investments, amounting to $5.56 billion in total liquid assets ($5.26B–$5.56B depending on short-term classification). 2. Capital Allocation & Share Buyback "Cannibal" Compounding

Concurrently with its Q4 FY2026 earnings release, EDU announced an aggressive $500 million total capital return package for FY2027 under its three-year shareholder return policy:

  • $300 Million Cash Dividend: Board-approved ordinary cash dividend to be distributed in two equal installments (December 2026 and June 2027). $200 Million Share Repurchase Program: Newly authorized 12-month open-market buyback program. This follows the near-complete execution of the prior authorization, where EDU repurchased 51.5 million common shares (~5.15 million ADSs) for $274.0 million through July 28, 2026.
Capital Allocation Synthesis: By combining $300M in direct cash dividends with $200M in share repurchases, EDU is returning over 60% of its annual Owner Earnings directly to shareholders. Buying back shares while the market heavily discounts the company's $4.71B net cash balance accelerates per-share Owner Earnings growth, shrinking the share count denominator and compounding intrinsic value per ADS.

Section 5: Warren Buffett Owner Earnings & Intrinsic Value Matrix

To establish an institutional-grade evaluation of New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. (NYSE: EDU), we apply Warren Buffett's 7-Pillar Intrinsic Value Framework, strictly rooted in first principles from Berkshire Hathaway’s Shareholder Letters. Rather than relying on speculative exit multiples or arbitrary Wall Street consensus, this model derives intrinsic equity value from normalized cash flow capability, balance sheet liquidity, and disciplined local hurdle discounting.

The 7-Pillar Intrinsic Value Framework Applied to EDU

1. Normalized Owner Earnings (1986 Shareholder Letter)

Buffett defines Owner Earnings as Operating Cash Flow minus Maintenance Capital Expenditures minus 100% of Stock-Based Compensation (SBC). In FY2026, EDU generated $885M in Operating Cash Flow. Deducting $95M in real dilution from SBC expense and $130M in Maintenance CapEx (necessary to maintain learning center footprints, IT infrastructure, and content development) yields Normalized Owner Earnings of $660M ($4.12 per ADS on 160M diluted ADSs). Crucially, Operating Cash Flow benefits from an interest-free customer float—students prepay tuition quarters in advance, expanding deferred revenue to $1.85B.

2. Mid-Cycle Normalization & Regulatory Pivot (1982 & 1991 Letters)

Following China's 2021 "Double Reduction" regulatory overhaul, EDU successfully pivoted away from K-9 academic curriculum tutoring into high-margin non-academic enrichment tutoring (1.07M sign-ups), high school test prep, overseas study consulting, smart learning hardware (326K users), and e-commerce/tourism via East Buy. FY2026 net revenues reached $5.66B (+15.5% YoY), with operating income jumping 50% to $643.3M. Cash flows are normalized across this post-pivot operating model rather than legacy pre-2021 peak figures.

3. Localized Country-Specific Sovereign Discounting (The PetroChina / Iscar Rule)

Valuing a Chinese enterprise using US 10-Year Treasury rates creates severe cost-of-capital distortions. We ground the hurdle rate strictly in the operational currency sovereign benchmark: China 10-Year Government Bond Yield (~1.71%) + 8.0% Equity & Geopolitical Risk Premium = 9.71% Discount Rate.

4. Capital-Light Moats & Expanding Cash Yield

EDU operates an asset-light, high-ROIC (>22% on operating capital) model. The initial Owner Earnings Yield stands at 7.30% ($4.12 Owner Earnings / $56.43 Market Price). Because pricing power in non-academic enrichment and test prep outpaces inflation, operating margins generate organic reinvestment runway without requiring heavy physical capital buildouts.

5. Share Buyback Cannibal Compounding (1999 & 2018 Letters)

Management implemented an aggressive $500M shareholder return program for FY2027 ($300M cash dividend + $200M new share repurchase authorization). By repurchasing shares at a discount to intrinsic value, management reduces the outstanding ADS count by 3.5% to 4.5% per annum, directly compounding per-share cash flow.

6. Balance Sheet Reality Bridge (Net Liquidity & Lease Adjustments)

EDU maintains an extraordinary capital fortress. Total cash, term deposits, and short-term investments total $4.85B against total contractual debt and lease liabilities of $0.85B. This leaves $4.00B in Net Cash & Liquid Investments ($25.00 per ADS), providing absolute balance sheet protection.

Buffett 5-Year Exchange Closure Assessment: If the NYSE closed trading for 5 years, an investor buying EDU at $56.43 would derive a 7.3% starting cash yield, supported by $25.00/ADS in pure cash holdings and double-digit organic growth in non-academic tutoring. The business generates sufficient internal cash to fully fund its $500M annual capital return program without taking on leverage.

Section 6: Execution Risk, Margin of Safety & Pre-Mortem Invalidation Triggers

A rigorous fundamental valuation must rigorously stress-test the thesis against management execution, regulatory headwinds, and macro vulnerabilities. Margin of safety is not merely a discount to fair value; it is balance sheet structural defense.

Execution Risk Evaluation:

  • Regulatory Risk (Medium-High): While EDU has compliant non-academic enrichment and high school tutoring operational frameworks, sudden policy updates from China's Ministry of Education regarding fee caps or operating hour restrictions pose constant latent risk.
  • East Buy Livestream Volatility (Medium): E-commerce and livestream content sales face low switching costs and key-opinion-leader (KOL) dependencies. Margin compression in East Buy could drag down non-GAAP consolidated operating margins.
  • Capacity Re-Expansion Execution (Low-Medium): Expanding physical learning centers in Top-tier cities requires discipline to prevent utilization rates and operating margins from dropping below target 7.2% levels.

Margin of Safety Assessment:

At the current market price of $56.43, EDU trades at a 27.6% discount to its Base Case Intrinsic Value ($78.00) and offers a $25.00/ADS net liquidity cushion. Liquid cash and short-term investments alone cover 44.3% of the total market capitalization. The market effectively values EDU's core education business—which generated $643M in FY2026 operating profit—at less than 8x normalized operating income.

Pre-Mortem Falsification Triggers (Thesis Invalidation Criteria):

  1. Deferred Revenue Breakdown: Deferred revenue growth turning negative YoY for two consecutive quarters, signaling deteriorating upfront student sign-ups and loss of brand moat.
  2. Regulatory Intervention on Non-Academic Services: Reclassification of non-academic enrichment courses under legacy K-9 academic restrictions.
  3. Capital Allocation Missteps: Cash drainage into dilutive non-core acquisitions that erode the current $4.85B cash fortress or cancellation of the $500M shareholder return commitment.
  4. Margin Contraction: Non-GAAP operating margin dropping below 5.0% due to unabsorbed expansion overhead or East Buy margin collapse.
